Yes Please explain any activities and/or experiences that demonstrate your commitment to the LGBTQ movement. Please be specific. From leading the charge in the Senate to repeal "Don't Ask, Don't Tell," to coming out as the first New York senator for marriage equality to championing equal protection and non-discrimination policies, I have worked throughout my career to deliver real results for New York's LGBTQ community. What's more, I know how to work across the aisle to get things done; I've passed bipartisan bills to take illegal guns o[ our streets, deliver health benefits to veterans and first responders, reform our military justice system and ban insider trading by members of Congress. Put simply, I have the experience and determination to get the job done. What are your policy priorities if you are to win this seat? How will these policy priorities impact the LGBTQ community? When I first came to Washington, LGBTQ+ individuals couldn’t get married, donate blood, or serve openly in the military. As a member of the Senate Armed Services Personnel Subcommittee I have become a leader in Congress in my fight for LGBTQ+ servicemembers. I was honored to work with the advocates to champion the repeal of the discriminatory Don’t Ask Don’t Tell policy. I was proud to put an end to it and to finally give our LGBTQ+ service-members the dignity and respect that they deserve. I have also fought for years to make sure transgender people can serve openly in our military. In addition to my leadership on these issues, I was also proud to push for allowing gay men to donate blood and to permit those living with HIV and HBV to serve in the military. And I have also worked to support LGBTQ+ businesses and protect against lending discrimination. Following Justice Clarence Thomas’ nasty opinion on the Supreme Court’s overturning of Roe v. Wade, I was proud to help galvanize Congress to pass the Respect for Marriage Act, which I cosponsored. I am also an original cosponsor of the Equality Act led by Senator Merkley, and have introduced two bills, the Hate Crimes Commission Act of 2021 and the John Lewis Every Child Deserves a Family Act, which would help expand protections for members of the LGBTQ+ community. 2
